results.name: Bishop Walter de Merton tomb d.1277
results.description:
Tomb of Bishop Walter de Merton (d.1277) in the north wall of the North Quire Transept of Rochester Cathedral. Bishop Walter was the founder of Merton College, Oxford. Stone and alabaster standing monument, consisting of a vaulted two bay canopy on clustered shafts. Restored in 1849, with a recumbent alabaster effigy, the third (1852, designed by R.C. Hussey, sculptor unknown). Enclosed by a C19th iron railing.  Behind are two small stained glass windows by Sir Ninian Comper. In adjoining bay is the slab from the earlier monument.  Brass plate on east wall refers to the 1849 restoration. Inscription on black marble tablet in slype refers to restoration of the tomb in 1662.

[Bibliography](https://rochestercathedralresearchguild.org/bibliography)

results.name: The Red Room, Russell Cotes Art Gallery & Museum
results.description:
> This room was originally Merton’s bedroom, decorated in his favourite colour. 
> 
> He and Annie had separate bedrooms with single beds (a common practice amongst middle-class couples of the time).The room was originally separated by a fretwork screen which created a sitting area in the room’s bay window.
>  
> The ceiling mural depicts the birth of the Roman goddess, Venus, and was intended to be viewed whilst lying in bed.

More information: https://russellcotes.com/the-red-room/

results.name: Eagle, George Jennings, 1890-1901
results.description:
From the collection of the Russell Cotes Art Gallery & Museum, Bournemouth, UK:
[russellcotes.com](http://russellcotes.com)

Ceramic or coade stone, South Western Pottery, Poole

"This eagle once stood in Annie [Nelson Clark] and Merton [Russel-Cotes]'s garden here at East Cliff Hall

It was made by George Jenning Southern Pottery Poole, (later Poole Pottery), possibly from ceramics or Coade stone (an artificial stone used for garden ornaments). Dated 1890-1901, similar eagles still guard the entrance to Poole Park. [view in [Google Maps](https://goo.gl/maps/9iRkxRuQMaP2)]

results.description:

He was also known as Bacchus (/ˈbækəs/ or /ˈbɑːkəs/; Ancient Greek: Βάκχος Bacchos) by the Greeks (a name later adopted by the Romans) for a frenzy he is said to induce called baccheia. ~ https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dionysus

South Park Gardens - Drinking Fountain
results.description:
A drinking fountain located within South Park Gardens, Wimbledon. Installed in 1904, this fountain was used by deliverymen who sold milk, coal and other domestic consumables to locals. The inscription on the base reads:

> MISS ELLEN REARDON'S REQUEST   
> IN MEMORY OF   
> HER FATHER MOTHER AND SISTER  
> DANIEL ELIZABETH AND MARGARET REARDON  
> 1880


> PRESENTED BY THE  
> METROPOLITAN DRINKING FOUNTAIN  
> & CATTLE TROUGH ASSOCIATION  

Captured in a 2 minute video in October 2023 with a Google Pixel 6 and processed in RealityCapture.

results.name: Deckelpokal (030005734001)
results.description:
Der silberne und vergoldete Deckelpokal wurde um 1900 in Frankfurt a.M. hergestellt. Dargestellt ist ein auf verschiedenen Erzen kniender Bergmann, sowie verschiedene unfertige Gravuren mit internationalem Bergbau-Bezug. Wahrscheinlich sollte er William Merton als Gründer der Metallgesellschaft AG in Frankfurt geschenkt werden. Es fehlt jedoch eine Inschrift, die dies einwandfrei belegen könnte.

The silver and gilt lidded goblet was made in Frankfurt a.M. around 1900. It depicts a miner kneeling on various ores, as well as various unfinished engravings with international mining references. It was likely intended as a gift to William Merton, the founder of the Metallgesellschaft AG in Frankfurt. However, there is no inscription that could prove this perfectly.

More Information: https://www.montandok.de/objekt_start.fau?prj=montandok&dm=Montanhistorisches+Dokumentationszentrum&ref=81469
